prerequisites: Basic knowledge of electronics technology, electronic components and controller systems

learning_outcomes.text: The student must review, analyze, and master the available course material.
The student formulates a design assignment in consultation with a potential client and determines, after analysis, the functional/electronic/mechanical requirements and specifications.
The student can search for additional information about the development environment, including manuals, tutorials, training videos, and can apply them to their project after analysis, if applicable.
The student uses their acquired theoretical knowledge, applies it during design, and can explain/defend the choices/implementation made.
The student can create a design using a schematic/Printed Circuit Board (PCB) design environment, datasheets, designer guides, application notes, or other relevant available information.
The student can select different components and interface them in the most appropriate way.
The student takes into account component vendor and/or producer-specific regulations and design rules, manufacturability, cost-effectiveness, testability, etc.
The student can create their own libraries in a clear/well-thought-out manner and use them to draw a readable and hierarchical schematic.
The student independently arrives at a clear schematic and a clever dual/multi-layer PCB design.
The student assembles their PCB step by step and performs the necessary partial tests to achieve a working whole.
The student can install the development environment and apply it in a future-oriented way (project/version management, SVN, Vault).

The student keeps track of their work/progress on TRAC or their own website and structuredly manages all other relevant information needed to document (datasheets, PDFs, calculations, etc.), understand, and explain their design.
The student can present their design, using a PPT, at the scheduled evaluation moment and defend their design choices.
The student creates a work plan based on the available information.
The student can process given feedback and evaluate their own work using available tools (ERC, DRC) and adjust their planning/work pace/strategy.
The student writes a concise technical report and creates an A4 Thomas More poster of their project.
The student submits the fully archived design/documentation electronically one week before the scheduled evaluation moment.
Each student creates an individual design but works together with the lecturer team and coaches other students.
The students work together so that their PCBs can be sent for fabrication, jointly by EmSys, in time (see detailed planning PCB fabrication).

syllabus_topics: Installing and Working with Altium Designer schematic/PCB design environment.
Creating and managing projects (Version management, Vault, SVN).
Schematic drawing: Basic settings for drawing schematics (grid, libraries ...).
Creation of schematic symbols, libraries and drawing of hierarchical schematics.
PCB drawing: Layer stack definition for dual/multi-layer PCBs, possibly flex PCB.
Setting manufacturer design rules.
Making footprint libraries and adding 3D bodies.
Definition of board size.
Routing, vias, repouring, interactive length tuning.
Import 3D.
DRC verification.
Output generation: BOM, Gerber, Drill, Documents (PDF), 3D export.
Submitting project data: Archived Altium Design, Production data, Structured documentation, Project PPT, A4 project Poster and Advanced PCB projects poster 2018-2019.
Assembly and testing: Formulating improvement points.
What is a PCB
PCB terminology
PCB structure and materials
PCB design
PCB manufacturing
Design issues
Assembly/Mounting: Applying solder pastes, Assembling the PCB, Necessary material for manual assembly, Machine assembly.
Soldering: Single/double-sided soldering and procedures, Soldering aids, Soldering problems.
Testing, inspection and post-treatment: Manual vs. automatic inspection, Different methods for testing, Post-treatments.
Packaging and protection: ESD issues, ESD protection, ESD solutions.
High density boards
Embedded components and wire bonding
Future technology

assessment_methods.method: Theory: Written exam with oral continuation

assessment_rules: The evaluation of the theoretical part is a written closed-book exam with closed questions and an oral continuation. For the lab evaluation, open questions are used, and the student may use all available information. Students who do not deliver a PCB design/realization cannot pass the course unit. A demonstrable and working PCB gives 'bonus points'. If a score of at least 10/20 is not achieved for any of the components, the student fails the entire course unit. For resits, students must contact the lecturers before the holiday period to discuss remediation, and must arrange for PCB fabrication themselves.
